title: How an MRI Scanner Works in 60 Seconds 🧲🩻 #shorts
description:
An MRI scanner wraps you in a superconducting magnet tens of thousands of times stronger than Earth's field, cooled by liquid helium to about -269 °C. It lines up the hydrogen in your body, knocks it with radio pulses, and listens to the signal it sends back. Gradient coils tag every spot so a computer can build a slice image. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#mri #science #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: An MRI magnet is about *30,000 times* stronger than Earth's magnetic field.

steps.label: Magnet
steps.text: It's a *superconducting coil*, chilled by liquid helium to about *minus 269* degrees.

steps.label: Protons
steps.text: Your body is full of *hydrogen*. Inside the magnet, those tiny protons *line up*.

steps.label: Radio pulse
steps.text: A *radio pulse* knocks them out of line. As they snap back, they *send a signal*.

steps.label: Gradients
steps.text: *Gradient coils* tweak the field spot by spot. That's the *loud knocking* you hear.

steps.label: Image
steps.text: A computer turns all those signals into a *slice image* of your body.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Magnet, radio, *picture*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
